system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:39:43 UTC, PROXY-HD-01 (10.30.20.30) initiated an SMB connection to FILE-HD-01 (10.30.20.20) on port 445. The inventory identifies PROXY-HD-01 as an explicit web proxy; this connection is unexplained by the supplied context and merits investigation, but its purpose is not established.

FILE-HD-01 made several HTTP connections to the proxy on port 8080 during the review period; the listed connections show exchanges measured in kilobytes, not evidence of a hundreds-of-megabytes transfer. They do not establish what the proxy forwarded externally.

At 13:37:22 UTC, DC-HD-01 recorded a certificate-preauthenticated Kerberos request for the FILE-HD-01$ account, with a certificate issued by Harbor Dental's enterprise CA. The record establishes the authentication event, but not its initiating process or purpose.

Records show WS-OHADDAD-01$ requesting a service ticket for FILE-HD-01 before the alert time, consistent with the supplied context that the administrator performs workstation patching from WS-OHADDAD-01. The ticket records alone do not establish that the documented patching procedure ran.

At 14:05 UTC, FILE-HD-01 connected to WS-OHADDAD-01 on TCP port 135. This direction differs from the described normal remote-administration initiation, but the connection record does not identify its purpose.

known_telemetry_limitations: FILE-HD-01 winsec and sysmon collection was unavailable from 13:30 through 14:10 UTC, including the alert time; process, logon, and command-line evidence for that interval is therefore missing.
PROXY-HD-01 proxy-log collection was unavailable from 13:30 through 14:10 UTC, so the destination, URL, and volume of any external transfer through the proxy cannot be determined from those logs.
Zeek connection, DNS, and SSL sensors are reported operational, but the supplied records do not identify an external destination or process for the reported bulk transfer.
claims_not_established: Whether the reported hundreds-of-megabytes transfer occurred as described, and its exact destination, content, and route.
Whether the transfer was made by the approved CobaltVault backup agent, another authorized process, or an unapproved process.
Whether the unexplained PROXY-HD-01-to-FILE-HD-01 SMB connection was authorized, malicious, or related to the reported transfer.
Whether the scheduled svc-claimsync password rotation occurred at 13:30 UTC, whether the job was updated, or whether its activity is related to the alert.
Whether the certificate-based authentication or FILE-HD-01-to-WS-OHADDAD-01 RPC connection was authorized or related to the reported activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover FILE-HD-01 process and security telemetry for 13:30–14:10 UTC, especially process creation, service activity, logons, and network-to-process attribution.
Obtain PROXY-HD-01 access and transaction logs for the interval, including client identity, requested host/URL, transferred byte counts, and any available TLS or destination metadata.
Obtain the original network-monitoring alert details and flow records, including exact start/end times, byte counts, destination IP/domain, and whether traffic traversed the proxy.
Verify CobaltVault agent execution and upload history, and compare its recorded transfer timing and volume with the alert.
Validate the 13:39 SMB connection from PROXY-HD-01 and the 14:05 RPC connection to WS-OHADDAD-01 against host, firewall, and administrator activity records.
Check change or job records confirming the svc-claimsync rotation and manual job update.
